lessons.title: Ratios & Unit Rates (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Solving Unit Rate Problems
lessons.reading: A rate compares two quantities with different units, like miles and hours. A unit rate tells the amount per 1 single unit (such as $6 per 1 pound). Divide the total amount by the number of units to find the unit rate.

principles.title: Computing Unit Rates by Division
principles.summary: Divide total cost or distance by quantity to find the rate per 1 unit.

assignment.scopeSummary: [Proportional Reasoning] Micro-Lesson Scope (~10 min total): Complete ONLY the 3 bite-sized steps below for "Computing Unit Rates by Division" (6.RP.A.2), then return to this tab for your randomized Mastery Check.

lessons.title: Percent of a Quantity (Part 2 of 2)
lessons.reading: Percent means "per 100." To find a percent of a number, rewrite the percent as a fraction over 100 (or a decimal) and multiply by the whole number.

principles.title: Calculating Percent of a Number
principles.summary: Express p% as p/100 and multiply by the base quantity.

lessons.title: Dividing Fractions by Fractions (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.reading: To divide by a fraction, multiply the first fraction by the reciprocal (flipped version) of the second fraction. Then simplify your answer to lowest terms.

principles.title: Dividing Fractions by Multiplying by the Reciprocal
principles.summary: Flip the second fraction and multiply numerators and denominators.

lessons.title: Solving One-Step Equations (Part 2 of 2)
lessons.reading: To solve an equation for x, use inverse (opposite) operations on both sides to get x by itself. Undo addition with subtraction, and undo multiplication with division.

principles.title: Solving Equations Using Inverse Operations
principles.summary: Undo addition or subtraction first, then divide by the coefficient of x.

lessons.title: Area of Triangles (Part 1 of 2)
lessons.reading: Every triangle is exactly half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height. Use the formula Area = (base × height) ÷ 2.

principles.title: Area of Right and Acute Triangles
principles.summary: Multiply base by height and divide by 2 to find triangle area.
